content:
Jony Ive and Sam Altman previewed a brand-new concept AI hardware device a year ago, generating huge expectations.

The latest reports suggest OpenAI may technically deliver on that promise, but it could end up competing to some extent with an upcoming AirPods model. If so, I can easily imagine AirPods Ultra being more popular...

The promise of OpenAI's hardware device

The pair previewed their AI hardware device in a video released last May. Details about the product's form factor were disappointingly scarce at the time, but the two did claim it would be something entirely new.

"I think this is going to be the coolest piece of technology that the world has ever seen." "So use your common sense — at least something should be beyond these legacy products." "I'm absolutely certain that we are at the前沿 of a new generation of technology that can make us all better versions of ourselves."

As I said at the time, you can't make promises like that and then end up launching something with a form factor we've all seen before.

A smart speaker equipped with cameras and sensors

We've certainly seen smart speakers before. But the latest reports suggest that is exactly what we should be expecting now. Bloomberg says the product's selling point is built-in cameras and other sensors.

Whether this truly represents an entirely new category of technology is debatable, but it's not hard to imagine such a device being far more capable than existing smart speakers.

But it may partially compete with AirPods Ultra

However, this combination — a device you can talk to, paired with cameras that let it sense its surroundings — is nothing new. Our iPhones already do this thanks to Visual Intelligence. Meta's smart glasses and competitors' products have already shown this. Ultimately, this sounds exactly like what we expect from the upcoming AirPods Ultra.

Of course, a speaker and earbuds aren't direct competitors, though there is some overlap in use cases. A smart speaker is more convenient at home — no need to stick something in your ears, and multiple people can use it at once. But OpenAI specifically mentioned the device would be portable, and I have to say, AirPods are far more convenient in form factor when out and about.

Maybe we'll be surprised in the end, but based on what we know now, I really can't imagine carrying a portable speaker around with me every day, except in situations where I already do — like wanting to listen to a nice song in a hotel room or holiday apartment on a weekend away. The promo video didn't quite say that, but I really can't see any scenario where I'd take it to a bar.

For me, AirPods Ultra seems to have far greater potential than a smarter speaker. What do you think? Take part in our poll and share your views in the comments.
